title: Ordinary derived coefficient-unit conversion cancels from scalar extension
statement: For a unital commutative-ring map φ:A→B and scheme T, scalar extension of the single-functor unit isomorphism at A, followed by ExceptionalCoefficients.unitIso at T and the inverse single-functor unit isomorphism at B, has exactly the same forward arrow as ExceptionalCoefficients.unitIso. This is an equality in the ordinary derived category, before applying site comparison.

proof.text: The inverse single-functor unit isomorphism is the identity by the existing unit-model theorem. Its hom-inverse identity gives the forward identity. Expand only the homs of isomorphism composition and functor mapIso. Scalar extension preserves the first identity and the target identity cancels, proving the ordinary scalar-unit equation. This holds for the zero ring and empty schemes as an identity of categorical unit maps.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryScalarUnitSandwich
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (T : Scheme.{u}) :
    ((Etale.scalarExtension φ T).mapIso
        (Etale.singleFunctorObjUnitIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T) ≪≫
      Etale.ExceptionalCoefficients.unitIso φ T ≪≫
      (Etale.singleFunctorObjUnitIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) T).symm).hom =
        (Etale.ExceptionalCoefficients.unitIso φ T).hom
